display_name: Sher Khan & Lad Malika of Chunar
one_line: Strategic partners who turned Chunar Fort and Bihar’s Ganges corridor into the launchpad of the future Sur Empire, c. 1528–1534 CE.

appearance.age_look: Sher Khan appears in his late 30s with a lean, battle-hardened build; Lad Malika appears in her early 30s with a poised, regal bearing.
appearance.face: Sher Khan has an oval face, warm medium-brown North Indian complexion, sharp aquiline nose, neatly trimmed black moustache and short beard, a thin scar along his left cheek, and an intense, calculating gaze with a default expression of calm, focused resolve; Lad Malika has a soft oval face, slightly lighter wheatish complexion, straight nose, arched brows, kohl-lined large anime-style dark eyes, and a composed, analytical default expression that suggests quiet authority rather than overt emotion.
appearance.hair: Sher Khan’s hair is straight, black, and shoulder-length, mostly hidden under a dark indigo quilted turban-like padded helmet with a narrow padded tail at the back; Lad Malika’s hair is long, straight, and black, parted in the middle, tied into a single thick braid that falls over her right shoulder, with a narrow red headband under a light cream dupatta that is pulled back from the face and pinned at the crown.
appearance.costume: Sher Khan wears early 16th-century North Indian Afghan-style martial dress: a long, sleeved, knee-length quilted coat (zaghul/qarqad-like) in deep indigo with subtle vertical stitching and a wrap-over front tied by a dark brown leather belt, over a dull red cotton under-tunic visible at the collar and cuffs, loose off-white cotton churidar trousers gathered at the ankles, and sturdy dark brown leather boots; over his torso he has a plain steel breastplate (char-aina style front plate only) strapped over the quilted coat, with no ornate engraving; his forearms are wrapped in brown leather bracers, and he wears minimal jewellery—just a simple iron signet ring on his right hand. Lad Malika wears an era-appropriate, modest North Indian noblewoman’s attire suited to fort governance rather than battle: a long-sleeved ankle-length kameez in muted marigold yellow cotton-silk with a subtle woven floral jaal pattern, a slightly flared hem and side slits to mid-thigh, paired with deep green churidar trousers; over this she wears a sleeveless, hip-length dark maroon brocade waistcoat (sadri) with small floral motifs in dull gold thread, kept open at the front; a light cream dupatta with a thin red border is draped over her head and shoulders but pulled back from the face, falling over both shoulders and down her back; she wears modest gold stud earrings, a single thin gold nose-ring without chain, and two slim gold bangles per wrist, with soft brown leather slippers on her feet.
appearance.signature: Sher Khan’s signature prop is a straight Afghan-Indian talwar-like sword with a slightly curved single-edged steel blade, a plain iron cross-guard, a dark brown leather-wrapped hilt, and a simple iron disc pommel, worn at his left hip in a dark brown leather scabbard; Lad Malika’s signature prop is an unrolled parchment map of the Ganges and Chunar region held in her left hand, with her right hand resting lightly on a small brass keyring of fort keys hanging from her waist sash.

ref_desc: Sher Khan is a lean, scar-cheeked Afghan commander in a deep indigo quilted coat with steel breastplate, indigo padded turban-helmet, off-white churidar, dark brown boots and a plain brown-hilted sword, beside Lad Malika in marigold kameez, maroon waistcoat, cream dupatta, green churidar and holding a Ganges map with brass keys.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two fixed characters from early 16th-century Bihar at Chunar Fort, shown together for consistent design: Sher Khan as a late-30s, lean, battle-hardened Afghan commander with medium-brown complexion, an oval face, aquiline nose, neat black moustache and short beard, a thin scar on his left cheek, and intense, calculating eyes, wearing a deep indigo quilted knee-length coat with vertical stitching over a dull red under-tunic, strapped under a plain steel breastplate, off-white churidar trousers, dark brown leather boots, brown leather bracers, and a dark indigo quilted turban-like padded helmet with a short padded tail at the back; he carries at his left hip a slightly curved steel sword in a dark brown leather scabbard, with a plain iron cross-guard, brown leather-wrapped hilt, and disc pommel, his stance alert and authoritative. Beside him, draw Lad Malika as an early-30s regal woman with wheatish complexion, oval face, straight nose, large dark anime-style eyes lined with kohl, and a calm, analytical expression; she has long straight black hair in a single thick braid over her right shoulder, secured under a narrow red headband and a light cream dupatta pulled back from her face and draped over head and shoulders. She wears a long-sleeved ankle-length marigold yellow kameez with subtle woven floral pattern and side slits to mid-thigh, deep green churidar trousers, and a sleeveless dark maroon brocade waistcoat left open, plus soft brown leather slippers, modest gold stud earrings, a thin nose ring, and a few slim gold bangles. In her hands she holds an unrolled parchment map of the Ganges and Chunar region, while a small brass keyring of fort keys hangs from her waist sash. Show them head-to-toe, front-facing, with clear visibility of their fixed hairstyles, garments, colours and props, emphasizing a dignified, historically grounded strategic partnership rather than romance.
